Free the diver using quadratic equations

On the Surface

The harbor lights reflect on the water. The diver surfaces, safe and sound: three gates, three equations, a single way out calculated step by step.

Time taken: 00:00

Trapped in the Submarine — Educational Escape Room · Quadratic Equations
Gate 1 · Forward Hatch

The First Lock

The flashlight beam sweeps over the rusted instruments beyond the inner porthole. The hatch is governed by a two-equation panel: solve both to work out the four-digit code.

x² − 5x + 6 = 0
x² − 11x + 28 = 0
Find the two solutions of each equation (four numbers in total) and sort them from smallest to largest. The code is the sequence of the four digits, with no spaces.
Gate 2 · Control Room

The Second Lock

The control panel is still running on emergency batteries: dim lights, flickering indicators. Reactivating the link to the surface requires a new code, hidden in two equations.

x² − 6x + 5 = 0
x² − 15x + 54 = 0
As before: find the four solutions and sort them from smallest to largest. The code is their sequence, with no spaces.
Gate 3 · Watertight Hatch

The Final Lock

The last door is the sturdiest of all. The mechanism isn't written in the usual form yet: before you can solve it, you'll need to rearrange the equation, moving all terms to the left of the equals sign.

x² + 3x − 10 = 5x − 2
Rearrange the equation into the form ax² + bx + c = 0, then find its two solutions.
Enter the code by writing the negative solution first (with a minus sign) and then the positive one, with no spaces. Example: if the solutions were −3 and 8, the code would be -38.
